scope: Reference-image BC1/BC3 and depth-transfer probe of the pinned Vulkan-wrapper candidate and its unpatched baseline against an independent CPU S3TC decoder, plus the system Vulkan loader as a native-driver decode cross-check. Offscreen transfer-only native probe; no app, APK, window, Wine, Steam or game is started. No phone/Adreno result is claimed.
label: emulator-llvmpipe-api36-4k

fixture_source_rule_summary: BC1/DXT1 block is 8 bytes: RGB565 c0, RGB565 c1 (little-endian), then 16 2-bit indices, LSB first, row-major inside the 4x4 block.
Endpoint components are UNORM: c/31 (red, blue) and c/63 (green) expanded to 8-bit with round-to-nearest.
c0 > c1: palette is [c0, c1, (2c0+c1)/3, (c0+2c1)/3]. Else: [c0, c1, (c0+c1)/2, transparent black (0,0,0,0)].
BC3/DXT5 block is 16 bytes: 8-byte alpha block, then an 8-byte BC1 colour block that ALWAYS uses the four-colour palette regardless of c0 vs c1.

All palette interpolants are exact rational weighted averages scaled to 8-bit and rounded to nearest with ties to even, the Vulkan/D3D float-to-UNORM convention. This is the convention the wrapper's compute-shader decoder implements; the emulator runs match it exactly (including a 42.5 tie that resolves to 42 on the driver).
Only UNORM BC1/BC3 are decoded here. BC7 decoding was judged not practical within this gate; its format support is still recorded. sRGB, BC2, BC4, BC5 and BC6 are not part of the required gate.

reference_decoder.language: python (pure stdlib, implemented for this tool)
reference_decoder.provenance: Original implementation from the S3TC/DXT1/DXT5 block-layout and palette rules documented in the Khronos Data Format / OpenGL EXT_texture_compression_s3tc family of specifications. No wrapper, bcdec or Mesa decoder code is reused; the wrapper's bcdec and compute-shader paths are the objects under test.
reference_decoder.license: same licence as this repository (original work)

cases.name: bc1 three-colour palette c0=blue c1=red (transparent index 3)
bc1 equal endpoints use three-colour mode
bc3 ignores colour endpoint order (always four-colour)
bc1 index order is LSB-first row-major
bc3 generator covers both alpha modes
d24s8 input values fit in 24 bits

generators.algorithm: Python random.Random(seed); block patterns cycle through four-colour, three-colour/transparent, equal-endpoint, all-black/all-white and random BC1/BC3 blocks so every palette branch and index range is exercised

limitations: Software Vulkan only: the emulator runs on llvmpipe (LLVMpipe) inside the Android emulator, not on Adreno/KGSL and not on a physical GPU.
No phone is attached to the qualifying machine. No Adreno, KGSL or physical-GPU result is claimed; the phone runbook is written but not executed.
Synthetic deterministic BC blocks, not game assets; no mip levels, array layers, sRGB variants or sub-block partial copies are exercised.
No graphics pipeline is created: the wrapper's decoded image is observed through buffer-image copies (and vkCmdBlitImage for the native driver decode), not through sampling or rendering.
No validation layers are loaded; correctness relies on probe metrics, not API validation.
BC7 decoding is not implemented in the independent reference; only BC7 format support is recorded. BC2/4/5/6 are likewise not part of the reference comparison.

Interpolated BC palette entries legitimately differ by a few LSBs between decoder implementations; the wrapper compute path matches the reference exactly, the wrapper CPU fallback (bcdec) is within 1 LSB and Mesa's native decoder within 2 LSB on this run, which is why a tolerance is reported alongside exact counts.
The pinned wrapper is a build-tree .so loaded via dlopen by the probe; it is not packaged, installed or selected by Vapor in this run.

Depth format reduction (WRAPPER_REDUCE_DEPTH_FORMAT) was deliberately not exercised: the required gate is create/bind/copy through TRANSFER_DST|TRANSFER_SRC, so depth images do not request DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage.

phone_runbook.status: written from the emulator-qualified tool; not executed here (no phone attached)
prerequisites: A phone with an Adreno GPU (KGSL / Qualcomm proprietary Vulkan driver) connected over adb and authorized.
Host: this checkout at base commit, NDK r27d at the recorded path (or pass --ndk), adb on PATH (or pass --adb).
Read-only pinned wrapper build directory containing candidate-stripped.so, baseline-stripped.so and native-probe/ auxiliary libraries.
Nothing needs to be installed on the phone: the probe and libraries are pushed under /data/local/tmp only.
commands: adb devices -l  # note the phone serial; only one device must be online or pass --serial
what_the_tool_does_on_the_phone: Compiles tools/tests/vulkan-wrapper-reference.c with NDK r27d aarch64-linux-android34-clang using 16 KB page-size link flags.
Pushes the probe, both pinned wrapper .so files and the native-probe auxiliary libraries to /data/local/tmp/vapor-wrapper-reference-2026-10-21, plus deterministic BC1/BC3/depth inputs.
Runs caps/copy/blit for the system loader, baseline and candidate with FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1 and the three decode configs (compute, compute-view, host-cpu).
Pulls readbacks, compares against the independent Python S3TC decoder, writes the evidence JSON and per-run logs.

controls_and_expected_outcomes.expected: device name is the Adreno driver, page_size matches getconf PAGE_SIZE (4096 or 16384)
compressed readback is byte-identical to the uploaded blocks
driver BC decode within the reported LSB tolerance of the reference; record exact and max-delta numbers
exact match to the independent reference; a nonzero exact mismatch is the finding to escalate
within 1 LSB (bcdec host fallback truncates BC3 alpha interpolants)
same pixel metrics; the candidate's fix concerns caller-owned format lists, not decode

controls_and_expected_outcomes.control: depth d16/d24s8/d32 copy on every target
controls_and_expected_outcomes.expected: bit-exact round trip; if a depth copy is unsupported by the phone driver, record the concrete VkResult/stage failure instead of claiming support

wrapper logcat shows 'Forcing BCn emulation' and the BC image is emulated (readback is expanded RGBA8). Note: this wrapper build still reports the underlying driver's textureCompressionBC in vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures, so that flag alone is not a forcing check.

what_to_record: Device model/hardware (ro.product.model, ro.hardware, ro.board.platform), Android release/SDK and page size.
Vulkan driver ID, driver name/info/version and apiVersion from the caps run; whether textureCompressionBC is native on the phone.
Per-run exit codes, RESULT lines, BYTES_OUT, readback sha256 and the per-mode mismatch metrics in the evidence JSON.
Wrapper logcat lines captured per BC run (they show which decode path ran: use_compute_shader=0/1, use_image_view=0/1).
Any depth image create/bind/copy failure with its stage and VkResult; do not infer depth support from the emulator run.
adjudication: PASS: all control runs pass; wrapper BC copy/blit metrics identical to the emulator run (compute exact, host-cpu within 1 LSB).
INVESTIGATE: exact mismatches appear only on the phone for the compute/view path, or max delta exceeds the tolerance; capture readbacks and logcat, and compare candidate vs baseline.
FAIL: rgba8 or compressed-transfer controls fail, or BC emulation is not observed (readback equals compressed input).
UNSUPPORTED: a depth copy fails on the phone driver; record it as a driver limitation, not a wrapper result.
do_not_claim: Do not report a phone/Adreno result until the phone run actually completes and its JSON is reviewed.
Do not use the emulator's llvmpipe numbers as Adreno/KGSL numbers.
Do not change existing repo files or commit while running the phone pass.

findings: Wrapper compute-shader decode (staging and image-view configs, candidate and baseline): 16/16 copy+blit probes match the independent reference decoder exactly (65536/65536 pixels byte-identical in the verified set).

Wrapper CPU fallback path (USE_CPU_BCN=all, bcdec): baseline/bc1 copy has 4094/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 1 LSB (bcdec truncates interpolated palette entries; within the reported tolerance).

Wrapper CPU fallback path (USE_CPU_BCN=all, bcdec): candidate/bc1 copy has 4094/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 1 LSB (bcdec truncates interpolated palette entries; within the reported tolerance).

Wrapper CPU fallback path (USE_CPU_BCN=all, bcdec): baseline/bc3 copy has 3308/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 1 LSB (bcdec truncates interpolated palette entries; within the reported tolerance).

Wrapper CPU fallback path (USE_CPU_BCN=all, bcdec): candidate/bc3 copy has 3308/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 1 LSB (bcdec truncates interpolated palette entries; within the reported tolerance).

System-loader native BC decode (vkCmdBlitImage, Mesa/llvmpipe): bc1 has 2999/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 2 LSB versus the reference, showing the expected inter-decoder convention spread; it is not the wrapper under test.

System-loader native BC decode (vkCmdBlitImage, Mesa/llvmpipe): bc3 has 1382/4096 pixels exact and a maximum channel delta of 2 LSB versus the reference, showing the expected inter-decoder convention spread; it is not the wrapper under test.
Candidate versus baseline: 16/16 comparable wrapper readbacks are byte-identical; the candidate's format-list ownership fix does not change decoded pixels.

Depth transfer: 9 depth probes (D16_UNORM, D24_UNORM_S8_UINT, D32_SFLOAT; system, baseline and candidate) are bit-exact round trips; buffer texel widths observed: d16=2 bytes, d24s8=4 bytes, d32=4 bytes.
Page size: probe sysconf=4096, getconf=4096, fixture ELF max-load alignment=16384 (16 KB link flags on a 4 KB-page emulator).

generation.note: The probe runs recorded here were executed by executing_tool_sha256 against fixture_binary_sha256; the JSON was then re-assembled by assembly_tool from the saved raw run payload (commands, environments, readbacks, metrics and per-run logs are unchanged). No device work was re-executed during assembly. The executing revision did not enable wrapper debug logging, so per-run wrapper logcat is empty; decode-path evidence is therefore limited to the recorded metrics/readbacks and to the wrapper knob semantics documented in protocol.wrapper_knobs_from_source (read from the pinned wrapper source).
